land.text: Peremyshl and the upper San-Dniester country, a Rus' town since 'Vladimir marched up the Lyachs and took their cities: Peremyshl, Cherven' (981, Primary Chronicle, Peremyshl page) and 'recaptured by Rus in 1031'

predecessors.note: The rus dossier's successor list does not name Peremyshl, and the page gives no date for the principality's founding ('Established: 11th century'); Cliopatria's first shape, 1056, is used.

land.text: Peremyshl, united in 1141 with Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod to form the Principality of Halych

successors.note: Cliopatria's Peremyshl row runs to 1146 and its Halych row begins in 1147 on the sum of the Peremyshl and Terebovlia shapes of 1139; this dossier ends in 1141 with the Peremyshl and Halych pages.

capitals.name: Peremyshl (Przemyśl)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Peremyshl. In 1141 Volodymyrko moved his residence to Halych (Halych page).

keyframe_review.note: 62,400 km2 for 1056-1065 on the upper San, Dniester and Tysa side of the Carpathians (21.4-27.3 E, 47.7-50.6 N). The infobox of the Peremyshl page gives 'Area: 1,124 km2' (ratio 0.018 to Cliopatria): that figure is not an area for a principality of this reach and is not used; the shape is kept. The page dates nothing in 1056-1086 ('first ruled by the Rostislavichi'; Ryurik Rostislavich, 'the earliest known prince', held the city in 1087), so the shape rests on Cliopatria.

62,000 km2: three cells fewer in the south (24.8-25.8 E, 47.8-48.5 N); no page event. Years corrected only: the shape holds 1066-1083 because Terebovlia is established 'around the year 1084' (Terebovlia page), taking the Terebovlia band out of Peremyshl in the 1084 keyframe.

New keyframe, one year: 'established as an appanage around the year 1084 and given to Vasylko Rostyslavych' (Terebovlia page, infobox 'Established: 1084'). Cliopatria draws the split from 1085 (51 cells, 24.4-27.1 E, 47.9-49.6 N, 50 of which are Cliopatria's Terebovlia shape of 1085); the 1085 shape is used from 1084.

48,600 km2 for 1085-1138. The Council of Liubech page (19 October 1097) gives 'Volodar and Vasilko Rostislavich: Peremyshl, Terebovl, and Cherven'; Cherven (the towns between the San and the Bug) is only partly inside the shape (it stops at 50.6 N) and no page opened gives its extent; kept. Peremyshl page: Volodar defended the city in 1097 against Yaroslav Svyatopolkovich and Coloman of Hungary.

correction.text: unchanged shape; holds 1139-1141, then it is the Principality of Halych

keyframe_review.note: 48,800 km2 for 1139-1146, the 1085 shape plus two cells. Years corrected: Peremyshl ends in 1141. Peremyshl page: 'Peremyshl was united with Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod to form the Principality of Halych' (1141); Halych page: 'In 1141, Volodymyrko moved his residence from Przemyśl to the more strategically located city of Halych, effectively establishing a unified Galician principality'. Cliopatria's Halych row starts in 1147 on the Peremyshl and Terebovlia 1139 shapes (425 cells against 423).

ledger.note: 1056: Peremyshl enters the map as a principality of its own, the Rostislavichi's land on the upper San (Cliopatria's first shape). The page is silent on the founding: 'Established: 11th century'; the Primary Chronicle 981 entry has Vladimir taking 'Peremyshl, Cherven and other towns', and the page has the city 'first ruled by the Rostislavichi'. Confidence 1: year is Cliopatria's.

1084: Terebovlia is carved out as an appanage for Vasylko Rostyslavych. 'established as an appanage around the year 1084 and given to Vasylko Rostyslavych'; Cliopatria's Terebovlia shape begins in 1085. The page does not say which principality it was taken from; the Cliopatria shapes show Peremyshl's.

1141: Peremyshl joins Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod in the Principality of Halych. 'Peremyshl was united with Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod to form the Principality of Halych' (1141); Volodymyrko moves his residence from Przemyśl to Halych.
1141: the Principality of Peremyshl ends in the unified Galician principality. The Halych page: Volodymyrko 'effectively establish[ed] a unified Galician principality'.

wars.name: Siege of Peremyshl (1097)
wars.outcome: Yaroslav Svyatopolkovich, allied with Coloman of Hungary, besieged the city, which Volodar defended; Davyd Svyatoslavich and his Polovtsy ally Bonyak defeated the Hungarians. No territory changed.
wars.note: The Council of Liubech (19 October 1097) confirmed Peremyshl, Terebovl and Cherven to Volodar and Vasilko Rostislavich; the page does not date the siege within 1097.

certainty.note: Carpathian and river frontiers with Hungary, Poland and the Cumans, never fixed by treaty or survey on the pages opened; the Cherven and Zvenyhorod marches are the softest.

sources.title: Principality of Peremyshl
sources.note: Identity, capital, the Rostislavichi, 1097 siege, 1141 union with Terebovlia and Zvenyhorod; infobox area 1,124 km2 (not usable).

sources.title: Principality of Terebovlia
sources.note: Terebovlia established c. 1084 as an appanage for Vasylko; united with Peremyshl in 1141.

sources.title: Council of Liubech
sources.note: Council of Liubech, 19 October 1097: Peremyshl, Terebovl and Cherven to Volodar and Vasilko Rostislavich.

sources.title: Principality of Halych
sources.note: 1141: Volodymyrko moves from Przemyśl to Halych; Zvenyhorod incorporated after 1145.

notes:
Start 1056 follows Cliopatria's first shape: the Peremyshl page gives only 'Established: 11th century' and no date for the founding, so the found event is confidence 1. The rus dossier's successor list does not name Peremyshl, and principality-of-volhynia (eu-16, starting 1054) may overlap the north of the 1056 shape; not checked.

Area: the infobox of the Peremyshl page says 1,124 km2, against Cliopatria's 62,400 km2 for 1056 and 48,600 for 1085; the infobox figure cannot be an area for a principality reaching from the San to the Tysa and is not used.

End 1141, not Cliopatria's 1146: the Peremyshl, Terebovlia and Halych pages agree on 1141 (the principality-of-terebovlia and principality-of-halych dossiers from eu-16-c and eu-16-d use 1141 too). Cliopatria's Peremyshl and Terebovlia rows run to 1146 and its Halych row starts in 1147, so the draw for 1142-1146 comes from the Halych dossier's new keyframes. Zvenyhorod 'was incorporated into the Galician lands' after Ivan Berladnyk's defeat in 1145 (Halych page), which no Peremyshl shape shows.

Terebovlia: the page puts its founding 'around the year 1084', Cliopatria's shape starts 1085; a one-year keyframe (_1084) bridges, as the Terebovlia dossier does.

Unsettled / not on a page opened: the Peremyshl princes between 1087 and 1141 (Ryurik Rostislavich 1087; Volodar and his sons; the pages give no dates for Volodar's death or for Vladimirko), the Rostislav Vladimirovich of Tmutarakan origin of the Rostislavichi, the 1099 Battle of the Wiar and Boleslaw III's campaigns, Hungarian and Polish frontiers (Kingdom of Hungary and Kingdom of Poland touch the shape 1056-1138 per the seed's neighbours list), Cherven's extent (the Cherven towns lie mostly north of the shape), and the lands south of the Carpathians that the 1056-1084 shape reaches (47.7 N). Pages that failed: none.

Region names needed: 'Cherven' (the Cherven towns between the San and the Bug) if a gap-filler adds them to the Peremyshl shape.
Page budget: Principality of Peremyshl, Principality of Terebovlia, Council of Liubech, Principality of Halych (4 of 5).
